cards.title: Distinction between Uncertainty and Variability in Translation
cards.claim: Uncertainty represents limited knowledge of the system and decreases as information accumulates, whereas variability is a property of the system (e.g., genetic/environmental) that does not decrease with larger sample sizes. In scaling, the primary concern is often the inherent uncertainty of the scaling methodology rather than the variability of preclinical input data.
conditions: Applicable when predicting human PK parameters from animal data.
Requires distinguishing between the uncertainty of the point estimate and the population variability of the parameter.
required_inputs: Point estimates of animal PK parameters (e.g., CL, Vss).
Explicit definition of the scaling method used.
Data on the source of error: methodological uncertainty vs. biological variability.
limitations: Does not provide a universal method for quantifying uncertainty; requires case-specific assessment.
Misinterpretation of uncertainty distributions as population variability can lead to incorrect safety margins.
cards.downstream_use: Use this distinction to correctly parameterize Monte Carlo simulations, ensuring that uncertainty distributions are not conflated with between-subject variability models.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Animal parameter uncertainty, scaling-method discrepancy and prospective human uncertainty

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
